title: Operations & Composition of Functions
summary: Functions combine by addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, and by composition $f(g(x))$ — feeding one function's output into another. Composition's domain excludes inputs that break either function.

inner function.plain: The one evaluated first in a composition.

composition domain.plain: Inputs valid for the whole composition.
composition domain.in_class: Must work in $g$ and then in $f$.

decompose.plain: Write a function as a composition.

concept_sections.heading: Arithmetic of functions
concept_sections.explanation: Combine functions pointwise: $(f\pm g)(x)=f(x)\pm g(x)$, $(fg)(x)=f(x)g(x)$, $(f/g)(x)=f(x)/g(x)$ where $g(x)\neq0$.
math_steps: Exclude zeros of the denominator for quotients.

concept_sections.heading: Composition
concept_sections.explanation: $(f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x))$: evaluate $g$ first, then apply $f$ to that result. Substitute $g(x)$ everywhere $f$ has an $x$.

concept_sections.heading: Order matters
concept_sections.explanation: In general $f\circ g\neq g\circ f$ — composition isn't commutative, so keep the order straight.
math_steps: Identify which is inner and outer.

concept_sections.heading: Domain of a composition
concept_sections.explanation: An input must be valid for $g$ and yield a value valid for $f$. Exclude inputs that break either step.

concept_sections.heading: Decomposing functions
concept_sections.explanation: To use the chain rule later, practice writing a complicated function as $f(g(x))$ — naming a natural inner piece.

problems.prompt: If $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=x-4$, find the domain of $f(g(x))$.
problems.hint: The inside of the root must be $\ge0$.
